assertion: MODT content does not change the stationary image.
origin: Candidate static-frame rule; the stronger derived-index interpretation was rejected by field/byte comparisons.
live_measurement: Three bases photographed with original, absent and foreign MODT in separate launches plus a repeat of the original: identical root world words; object pixels differ no more than between the two original launches once the whole-frame brightness offset between launches is removed.
reason: Supported for three static models at close range. Distance, streaming and memory-pressure effects were not tested.

assertion: BGSM/BGEM factors use the NIF AlphaFunction numbering for the three enabled tuples.
origin: Candidate equation; nifxml documents AlphaFunction but no permitted source equates BGSM numbering.
live_measurement: Photograph the three tuples over known background; compare source/destination contributions and transparency.

assertion: Stored radians produce row rotation Rx(x)*Ry(y)*Rz(z); world point is t+s*R^T*p.
origin: Initial Euler candidate; disproved by independently measured multiaxis roots.
live_measurement: Measure world matrices for X/Y/Z 30-degree and combined XYZ placements; compare every coefficient before photo fitting.
reason: reviewed measurement decision: independent reproduction established 39 controlled measurement roots with Rz*Ry*Rx; Rx*Ry*Rz fails multiaxis.

assertion: ACTI/DOOR/STAT bases with the IsMarker bit are hidden.
origin: Reviewed photographs of flagged ACTI/DOOR/STAT specimens and an unflagged shared-model control.
live_measurement: Flagged ACTI, DOOR and STAT controls absent in photographs; the unflagged shared-model twin is visible.
reason: Support covers the base bit for those three record types; no node-name inference.

assertion: An absent REFR.XSCL contributes unit reference scale; absence stays preserved.
origin: Explicit hypothesis registered before interpreting absent XSCL; six-base raw-word control.
live_measurement: Six bases, 18 raw transforms: absent XSCL and explicit 1.0 both 3F800000; explicit 0.5 is 3F000000.
reason: Absence remains represented explicitly in the source view.

assertion: ONAM/DATA constituent instances reproduce the static SCOL frame; generated MODL is retained as an alternative, not drawn a second time. Constituent Euler uses refr_rotation_zyx_v2 provisionally; not measured separately.
origin: Candidate source of static geometry; both generated MODL and ONAM/DATA parts remain preserved.
live_measurement: Compare loaded SCOL geometry, material bindings and world matrices with transformed constituent NIFs; any visual or geometric difference rejects equivalence.

assertion: An absolute drive-prefixed citation resolves after its last complete data component, only to one available VFS winner.
origin: Prospective unique-winner resolution rule, registered before lookup and photo comparison.
live_measurement: Controlled object with an absolute Data-prefixed citation appears textured.

assertion: A rootless citation receives its citation-type root, only if exactly one available VFS winner exists.
origin: Prospective citation-root completion with a unique existing VFS winner.
live_measurement: Weak sample: rootless-citation specimen is only available in an unqualified cropped capture.
reason: Supported with weak evidence; preserve this sample limitation.

assertion: The candidate winding and raw material/NIF double-sided declarations predict which triangle faces contribute pixels.
covered_causes: cull option only; never readiness release
origin: Candidate winding plus preserved material/NIF sidedness declarations.
live_measurement: Single-sided sign photographed close from both sides in one launch, in two placements: drawn from the front, absent from the back. The two-sided case is unmeasured: the glass specimen was invisible from both sides.
reason: Half measured. A visible two-sided specimen is needed before the rule can be supported.

assertion: A NIF scene geometry label EditorMarker followed by ASCII decimal digits and/or colon plus decimal digits denotes an editor helper under the existing marker-hiding hypothesis.
origin: Prospectively registered decimal-label interpretation, distinct from the base marker bit.
live_measurement: One mixed ordinary/helper model photographed and drawn with and without the suffixed subtree: the photograph matches the drawing without it.
reason: Supported with one model. The label pattern is the measured scope.

assertion: Measured convention: row M=Rz(z)*Ry(y)*Rx(x), world point t+s*M^T*p; no bit-exact arithmetic claim.
origin: Independent raw-matrix reproduction; restricted earlier fixture and subsequent multiaxis counterchecks.
live_measurement: Fourteen measured roots; unique among 24 order/sense/storage candidates below 1e-5; max error 2.1e-7, runner-up 1.43.
reason: Convention supported; exact arithmetic remains open in rotation-arithmetic.md; only identity matches all 13 words.

assertion: Citation starting with complete data/ component uses its remainder, only with a unique existing VFS winner.
origin: Prospective Data-relative resolution prediction frozen before VFS lookup.
live_measurement: Controlled object with a Data-relative citation appears textured.

live_measurement: Compare instance032 and Bench2 light/dark controls; unsupported falloff/grayscale/refraction/soft effects remain refused.
reason: Multiplication, interpolation and transfer are a rendering hypothesis; field layout alone does not establish the engine equation.

assertion: Exact EditorMarker names identify hidden NIF helper subtrees under the former combined visibility rule.
origin: Exact-name assertion kept independent of the measured record marker bit.
live_measurement: One mixed ordinary/helper model photographed and drawn with and without the named subtree: the photograph matches the drawing without it.
reason: Supported with one model. Exact EditorMarker name only.

assertion: A BSTriShape whose exact AVObject name is VisibilityEditorMarker:0 is omitted as editor helper geometry; raw data remains available.

live_measurement: One measured interior with four placements of two shrub models: the helper boxes drawn from this mesh are absent in the photographs.
reason: Supported with a small sample (two models, one cell). Narrow literal label only.

assertion: Transposing the nine column-major NIF rotation words gives the comparable three SDK dump storage rows for stationary local transforms. Equivalently, the nine words are the rows of a matrix acting on column vectors (a node maps a child point p to t + s * R * p); the static renderer (Transform::from_fields) and the actor rest pose both read them so.
covered_causes: analysis_only; reading of Transform::from_fields (static render, bounds, collision frames); no readiness change
origin: Prospectively announced after local-word differences exposed a storage-order confound; nifxml describes column-major data and dump documentation describes three stored rows without a composition convention. Offline (spec/nif.md, Node rotation words): over the base records whose model box differs by more than 1 unit between the two readings, the record's OBND is within 1.01 of the box of the row reading only for 327 and of the column-major reading only for 2 (436 both, 372 neither; root transform applied or not); the moved shapes lie inside OBND under the row reading only for 343 records and the column-major reading only for 32; skeleton NIF bones match the bone nodes of their addon models for 111,574 of 118,050 under the row reading and 4,217 under the column-major one (spec/actor.md).
live_measurement: Compare both storage orders for all 94 uniquely matched node locals in two pauses; retain raw words, 18 nonunique requests and independent changing nodes. Offline point evidence (OBND boxes, skeleton bones) moved the renderer to the row reading; photograph one placed model with a shape under two non-commuting node rotations beside its drawing: the other reading must misplace that shape.
reason: Pending: the renderer change rests on offline evidence; no live measurement of nested node rotations yet.

origin: Candidate from the nifxml class descriptions (Fallout 4 Collision Object/System) and the collision census; no permitted source states runtime collision.
live_measurement: In one purpose-built interior, place a STAT whose model has a physics system and a STAT whose model has none; walk the player into each and record whether the player position stops at the surface or passes through. Repeat in a second launch.

assertion: Body ID of a bhkNPCollisionObject selects one body inside its bhkSystem payload, the one driven by or driving the Target node.
covered_causes: bhkNPCollisionObject.Body ID with several objects on one system

live_measurement: In a model with several objects on one bhkPhysicsSystem, displace each body in the running game (hit or push it) and record which node's runtime transform follows; every Body ID must map to its own Target node.

assertion: Havok collision coordinates (decoded vertices, record points, centres, radii, body and compound translations) times 69.99125 are world (render) units.
covered_causes: fo4-havok shape coordinates placed by fo4_scene::collision
origin: Stored-byte census: render/collision extent ratio mode about 69.991 over 10,893 bodies with identity placement (spec/havok-mesh.md, Units). Measured for one convex polytope box by live run C1 2026-11-21 (this installation only): its top rests at 176 at reference scale 1 and 352 at scale 2, matching 69.99125 and excluding 70. Other shape classes (compressed mesh, sphere, capsule, compound) unmeasured.
live_measurement: Repeat the box measurement for a compressed mesh, a sphere, a capsule and a compound: predicted contact height = reference z + 69.99125 x stored height x scale; a residual larger than the gap between the 69.99125 and 70 predictions, or a different factor for any class, refutes it.

assertion: A body's shape is placed in the frame of the Target node of the bhkNPCollisionObject that names it: the reference's ZYX placement and scale (as for the render mesh), then every SCOL part placement, then the file's node transforms from the footer root down to the Target, composed exactly as the render walk composes them; it rotates and scales with the reference in the same sense as the render mesh.
covered_causes: bhkNPCollisionObject.Target node chain; REFR DATA/XSCL applied to collision
origin: Candidate from the render convention (refr_rotation_zyx_v2, NIF node composition). live run C1 2026-11-21 (this installation only): reference scale applied (scales 1, 2 and 3) and rotation in the render sense for a convex polytope; the file node chain is indicated, not proven.
live_measurement: Rest an object on a model whose Target is a child node with a stored translation and rotation, at several reference rotations and scales, and read the runtime contact position; any node composition other than the render one that fits better refutes it.

assertion: Level 'ignored' of the open body placement rule: the translation (body bytes 48) and four f32 (body bytes 64) stored in a body element do not move its shape; the shape sits in the Target frame as stored. Default level.
covered_causes: hknpPhysicsSystemData body translation and rotation, non-identity
origin: live run C1 2026-11-21 (this installation only): measured for a convex polytope slab whose body stores a translation (the rest pose matches 'ignored'); only indicated for compressed meshes. Exclusive with havok_body_placement_applied_v1.
live_measurement: Rest or drop an object on a compressed-mesh body and on a compound body that store a non-identity translation or rotation and read the runtime contact pose; compare with both levels from fo4-unpack cell-collision. A pose that matches 'applied' and not 'ignored' refutes it.

assertion: Level 'applied' of the open body placement rule: the body's four f32 at bytes 64, read as x, y, z, w (w last) of a unit quaternion, rotate the shape actively and the three f32 at bytes 48 translate it, in collision units, inside the Target frame and before the unit factor.
covered_causes: hknpPhysicsSystemData body translation and rotation, non-identity
origin: Candidate reading of the stored body element (spec/havok-bodies.md). live run C1 2026-11-21 (this installation only): contradicted for a convex polytope slab (the stored translation did not move it); the order w, x, y, z was refuted, the order otherwise open. Exclusive with havok_body_placement_ignored_v1.
live_measurement: Same measurement as havok_body_placement_ignored_v1: a pose that matches 'ignored' and not 'applied' refutes it for that class; a pose matching neither refutes both.

assertion: An instance of hknpStaticCompoundShape or hknpDynamicCompoundShape places its child as p' = t + s R(p), where the three stored rows are the images of the child's x, y and z axes (the fo4_scene Transform convention), t the stored translation and s the stored scale (three equal values).
covered_causes: compound instances with a non-identity rotation, translation or scale
origin: Candidate from the stored instance layout (orthonormal rows, positive determinant, equal scale values; spec/havok-bodies.md). Rows against columns is not decided by the bytes.
live_measurement: Rest an object on a model whose dynamic compound has an instance with a non-identity rotation, in a purpose-built interior, and read the contact position; the transposed rotation must predict worse. Instances with the identity rotation do not decide it.

assertion: hknpScaledConvexShape places its child's points at scale * p + translation per axis (stored scale at byte 64, translation at byte 80).
origin: Candidate from the stored layout (three positive scale values, three translation values; spec/havok-bodies.md). The order of scale and translation and the effect on a capsule radius are not decided by the bytes.
live_measurement: Rest an object on a model whose body is a scaled convex with unequal scale values or non-zero translation and read the runtime contact height and extent; the other order (scale after translation) must predict worse.

assertion: The triangles [a, b, c] and, for quads, [a, c, d] decoded from hknpCompressedMeshShape primitives lie on the surface the game's collision uses for that shape; vertex records are left out of the triangle set. Which side of a triangle blocks is not part of this rule.
origin: The split and winding coincide with the render mesh in the measured files (spec/havok-mesh.md, Triangles). live run C1 2026-11-21 (this installation only): in a two-plane mesh the upper plane was passable from above, so sidedness is open; triangles are exposed with their stored winding and normal.
live_measurement: Rest an object across a non-planar quad of a measured mesh, from above and from below, and read the runtime contact height along the quad; heights following the [b, d] split, or passing through from the side the winding faces, refute or narrow it.

assertion: The f32 at byte 20 of hknpConvexPolytopeShape is a radius added to the surface: the collision surface lies that far (in collision units, scaled with the placement) outside the hull of the stored vertices.
origin: The f32 is finite and not negative in every measured polytope (spec/havok-objects.md). live run C1 2026-11-21 (this installation only): a convex polytope slab rests at 96.000, not at 95.300, with the radius added, and the radius scales with the reference. One object class; the face set of the hull is not read.
live_measurement: Rest an object on polytopes with different stored radii at reference scales 1 and 2 and read the contact heights; a height that ignores the radius, or a radius that does not scale with the reference, refutes it.

assertion: A material swap (MSWP, its conditional filter FNAM included) does not change the collision of the reference or base that names it: the collision is that of the model as stored, placed by the reference.
covered_causes: MSWP named by REFR.XMSP or by a base model; DeletedMaterialSwap, MissingMaterialSwap, RuntimeMaterialSwapFilter and the swap material citations, for collision only (fo4_scene::readiness)
origin: No source states it; this project reads material swaps for rendering only. Motivated by a live drop comparison in one interior cell (2026-11-21, this installation only): with the collision of one static collection whose reference carries a filtered material swap placed, 34 of 38 settled player heights agree with the vertical-ray collision surface within 0.05 units, against 8 of 38 without it. One reference and one swap; an indication, not a measurement of the rule.
live_measurement: In one purpose-built interior, place two references of one static model with collision, one with a material swap that carries a filter (FNAM) and one without; drop the player from one height over matched points of both and walk into the same face of each, in two launches. A difference in settled player.getpos z or in stop distance between the two refutes it.

assertion: The collision of a model is the same whether or not its render-only inputs are present, readable or interpreted: material and texture files and their citations, shader, effect and material fields, light data, skinning and the visibility of editor-marker geometry.
covered_causes: Render-only blockers of a reference other than its material swaps (spec/collision-placement.md, Collision readiness), for collision only (fo4_scene::readiness)
origin: No source; the collision decoder reads none of these inputs. Registered with mswp_collision_unchanged_v1 after the same live drop comparison.
live_measurement: Through an overlay plugin, place one model with collision twice in one interior: as shipped, and as a copy whose material citations name missing files; drop the player over matched points of both and walk into both, in two launches. A difference in settled player.getpos z or in stop distance refutes it.

assertion: The terrain of an exterior CELL is the single winning, non-deleted LAND record among that CELL's child groups (kinds 8, 9 and 10, observed in the temporary group 9); a cell with none has no terrain and a cell with two or more is refused.
origin: UESP Skyrim group table lists LAND among records found only in subgroups; which cell group and how many per cell is not stated for Fallout 4.
live_measurement: Offline: census of every exterior cell (LAND count and group kind per cell). Live: stand on ground in a cell whose LAND an overlay plugin deletes or duplicates and record whether the ground disappears or which copy is used.

assertion: VHGT heights accumulate in stored order, 33 rows of 33: the first value of each row adds to a running column sum started at the f32 offset; every other value adds to its western neighbour in the same row.
origin: UESP Skyrim and Oblivion LAND pages (reconstruction text and snippet; bytes signed, while fopdoc's Fallout 3 page types them unsigned); not stated for Fallout 4.
live_measurement: Offline: equality of heights across the shared edge of adjacent cells against the transposed and mirrored alternatives. Live: player.getpos z after settling at several x,y in one exterior cell; heights must match within the step of one vertex.

assertion: One unit of the VHGT offset and of each accumulated signed byte is 8 world units of height.
origin: UESP Skyrim and Oblivion LAND pages, stated there as assumed from Oblivion; not stated for Fallout 4.
live_measurement: Offline: lowest collision point of placed objects against the ground under them, for factors 4, 8 and 16. Live: player.getpos z after settling at several x,y of an exterior cell.

assertion: Row 0 of the 33 x 33 grid is the southern edge (smallest y) and column 0 the western edge (smallest x); rows advance north (+y), columns east (+x).
origin: UESP Skyrim LAND page (row 0 south, column 0 west; bottom-left start); not stated for Fallout 4.
live_measurement: Offline: edge continuity under the eight symmetries of the square; objects against ground. Live: player.getpos at the four corners of one exterior cell with distinct heights.

assertion: Vertex (row r, column c) of the cell with XCLC grid (X, Y) lies at world x = 4096 X + 128 c, y = 4096 Y + 128 r: 32 quads of 128 units over a 4096-unit cell whose south-west corner is at 4096 times the grid coordinates.
origin: UESP Skyrim LAND page (128-unit lattice over a 4096 x 4096 footprint); placement of the cell corner at 4096 times XCLC is not stated by a source.
live_measurement: Offline: objects against ground; continuity only holds if neighbours share edges at these positions. Live: player.getpos at a cell corner and at the centre of a quad.

assertion: Level 'sw_ne' of the open diagonal rule: each 128-unit quad is split along its south-west to north-east diagonal into [SW, SE, NE] and [SW, NE, NW].
origin: Candidate; no source states how the game triangulates a quad.
live_measurement: Live: player.getpos z after settling at the two off-diagonal points of a non-planar quad; the other level must predict worse. Offline: objects against ground under both levels.

assertion: Level 'nw_se' of the open diagonal rule: each 128-unit quad is split along its north-west to south-east diagonal into [SW, SE, NW] and [SE, NE, NW].
origin: Candidate; no source states how the game triangulates a quad.
live_measurement: Same measurement as the sw_ne level.

assertion: Against static collision the player is a vertical capsule of radius 16 world units (fo4_walk::Params::PROVISIONAL, a placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.
live_measurement: Walk the player into a placed box whose collision face plane is known and into a thin vertical pole; record player.getpos x/y when stopped in each of two launches. Face distance and pole-axis distance both equal the radius if the shape is a vertical capsule.

assertion: The player's capsule is 128 world units tall from the feet to its top (placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.
live_measurement: Place slabs over a corridor at decreasing clearances (e.g. 140, 132, 128, 124, 120 units above the floor); record the lowest clearance the player walks under, standing, in two launches.

assertion: The first-person camera sits 120 world units above the feet (placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.
live_measurement: Standing on a floor of known height (player.getpos z), look level at markers of known height on a far wall; the marker on the screen's centre row gives the eye height. Repeat at two distances.

assertion: The player walks onto a ledge up to 20 world units high without jumping, and follows drops up to 20 units without leaving the ground (placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.

assertion: The player walks up surfaces up to 45 degrees from horizontal and cannot walk up steeper ones (placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.
live_measurement: Ramps of placed boxes rotated 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55 and 60 degrees; record the steepest one the player walks up and whether he slides down the next, in two launches.

assertion: The player falls with constant acceleration 9.81 m/s^2 times 69.99125 units per metre, about 686.6 world units/s^2, with no terminal speed (placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder: Earth gravity times the pending unit rule havok_collision_units_69_99125_v1 (spec/walk.md).
live_measurement: Walk off ledges of known heights (64, 256, 1024 units) and time the fall to landing from frame captures at a known frame rate, or sample player.getpos z; compare with 0.5 g t^2.

assertion: Walking moves the player at 100 world units per second on level ground (placeholder).
origin: Provisional placeholder of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.
live_measurement: Walk straight between two markers a known distance apart on level ground; time it from frame captures and record player.getpos at both ends, in two launches.

assertion: Running moves the player at 350 world units per second on level ground (placeholder).

assertion: In the air the player's horizontal velocity keeps the value it had when he left the ground; movement input does not steer it.
origin: Provisional choice of the first walking controller (spec/walk.md); no source.
live_measurement: Walk off a high ledge and, once in the air, hold the opposite direction; compare the landing point (player.getpos) with the one reached without input, in two launches.

assertion: For the walking controller every compressed-mesh triangle blocks the player from both sides, whatever its stored winding.
origin: Provisional choice of the first walking controller; sidedness is open in havok_mesh_triangles_surface_v1 (one plane of a two-plane mesh was passable from above).
live_measurement: Stand on and under single-plane mesh surfaces of both windings (normals up and down, from the cell-collision report) and walk or jump into them from each side; record where player.getpos stops.

assertion: LAND quadrant q (BTXT/ATXT byte 4) covers the 17 x 17 vertices of rows 16 floor(q/2) to 16 floor(q/2)+16 and columns 16 (q mod 2) to 16 (q mod 2)+16 of the 33 x 33 grid: 0 south-west, 1 south-east, 2 north-west, 3 north-east; neighbouring quadrants share their edge vertices.
origin: UESP Skyrim LAND page names quadrants 0 bottom left, 1 bottom right, 2 upper left, 3 upper right; not stated for Fallout 4 or as a vertex range. Offline indication (this installation, all LAND records): per-texture weights on vertices shared by two quadrants of a cell agree within 2.5/255 for 84.3% of 322,445 shared pairs with both bases present, 51.4% or less for the two mirrored mappings and 21.2% or less for the five others; the layout and the VTXT position mapping are tested together.
live_measurement: Top-down screenshot of a cell whose four quadrants have distinct base textures: each texture must fill the predicted 2048-unit square; player.getpos at the texture boundaries.

assertion: VTXT position p (0 to 288) is the quadrant-local vertex in row floor(p/17), column p mod 17, rows north and columns east as in land_grid_origin_southwest_v1; a vertex no VTXT entry names has opacity 0 for that layer.
origin: UESP Oblivion LAND page: u16 position 0 to 288 in a 17 x 17 quadrant grid, row order not stated for Fallout 4. Offline indication (this installation): within-cell quadrant seams as in land_quadrant_layout_v1; across cells, per-texture weights on the shared edges of 304,007 vertex pairs agree for 80.6% under this mapping and 49.2% or less under the seven other symmetries of the grid. Positions above 288 and repeated positions within one layer: none in 8,246,713 entries.
live_measurement: Paint a test cell whose one layer has a known asymmetric opacity pattern (an L shape) and photograph it from above; the pattern must appear where this mapping places it.

assertion: A VTXT opacity is the final weight of its layer's texture at that vertex; the base texture's weight is 1 minus the sum of the layer opacities at the vertex (0 where the sum exceeds 1); weights are interpolated linearly across each triangle and the colour is the weighted sum of the textures' colours, texture alpha unused. Layer order does not change the colour.
origin: Candidate; no source states the blend. Offline indication (this installation): the layer opacities of a quadrant sum to at most 1 at all but 61 of 9,087,604 vertices (an over-composition would routinely exceed 1); every opacity is a multiple of 1/255; within-cell seam agreement is 84.3% with these weights against 80.2% for ascending over-composition and 80.1% for descending. ATXT layer numbers of every quadrant are contiguous from 0 and stored ascending (173,928 quadrants).
live_measurement: Photograph, from above and in one launch, a vertex where two layers of distinct flat colours have opacities 0.5 and 0.5 over a third base colour: the base must not show; repeat at 0.25 and 0.25: base 0.5.

assertion: A quadrant without BTXT has a base texture that no record names (the default), and an ATXT whose texture FormID is zero names the same default; its weight follows land_layer_weights_residual_v1. Which texture the default is is not stated by the data: land_default_texture_world_named_v1 names a candidate where accepted, and it stays refused otherwise.
origin: Candidate. Offline indication (this installation): 140,298 of 173,928 quadrants have no BTXT and no ATXT, 5,733 have ATXT and no BTXT, 6,934 ATXT have FormID 0; no WRLD subrecord resolves to an LTEX. On 32,299 seam vertex pairs where one quadrant lacks a base and the default has a non-zero weight, replacing that default by the neighbour's FormID-zero layer makes the weights agree in 16,770 pairs, by any single LTEX in at most 1,147.
live_measurement: Photograph a quadrant without BTXT and a quadrant whose ATXT has FormID 0 at full opacity in one launch: both must show one and the same texture.

assertion: The 4-byte TNAM of an LTEX is a FormID naming the TXST that draws the landscape texture, and TX00 of that TXST is its colour texture; a TXST without TX00 (material only) is refused unless ltex_texture_set_material_diffuse_v1 is accepted.
origin: Candidate from the stored data; no source for Fallout 4 LTEX. Offline indication (this installation): every one of 128 winning LTEX has one 4-byte TNAM resolving to a TXST; every BTXT (27,897) and every non-zero ATXT but one (91,603) resolves to an LTEX. Of the 128 TXST, 96 have TX00 (all ending _d, BC1 or BC3, 1024 or 2048 wide), TX01 (_n, BC5) and TX07 (_s, BC5); 32 have no textures and an MNAM material.
live_measurement: Photograph a cell whose quadrant uses a landscape texture with a distinctive TX00 and compare with the same cell after an overlay plugin points the TNAM at another TXST.

assertion: A landscape colour texture repeats every 256 world units in x and y, aligned with the cell's south-west corner (16 repeats per cell); u grows east and v south (the image's first row toward north). Placeholder.
origin: Placeholder; no source states the repeat. Offline indication only: the placed objects of one exterior cell have an area-weighted median of 0.148 world units per full-resolution texel (quartiles 0.100 and 0.188), which for a 2048-texel landscape texture is a repeat of about 303 units; 256 is the nearest whole number of quads. The image's mirror is not decided by the data.
live_measurement: Top-down screenshot of flat ground with a distinctive landscape texture at a known camera height: count repeats over a known distance (player.getpos at two marks) and check the image's orientation.

assertion: VCLR stores one RGB byte triple per vertex of the 33 x 33 grid in the VHGT frame; each byte divided by 255 multiplies the textured colour at that vertex, interpolated like the weights, in the stored (encoded) colour values.
origin: UESP Oblivion LAND page: 24-bit RGB per vertex filled from the bottom left; the multiplication is a candidate. Offline indication (this installation): on shared cell edges with VCLR on both sides, 68,705 of 69,149 non-white vertex pairs are byte-equal in this frame against 47.2% or less under the other symmetries; 151,456 shared pairs are white on both sides.
live_measurement: Photograph ground of one texture across a VCLR gradient and the same ground in a copy of the cell with VCLR removed by an overlay plugin; the ratio of pixel values must follow the stored bytes.

assertion: A texture set (TXST) with no TX00 and an MNAM material path draws a landscape texture whose TNAM names it with the diffuse texture of that material, which must be a lighting material (BGSM); its UV and tiling fields are not applied. A material that is not a BGSM, has an empty diffuse path or does not resolve is refused.
origin: Candidate from the stored data; no source for Fallout 4 LTEX. Offline indication (this installation): 32 of 128 winning LTEX name one of 18 distinct TXST that have no TX00 and an MNAM; all 18 materials are BGSM files whose diffuse path resolves to a texture that decodes.
live_measurement: Photograph a cell whose ground uses such a landscape texture, then the same cell after an overlay plugin points the TXST's MNAM at a copy of the material whose diffuse is a distinctive test texture: the ground must change with it, in two launches.

assertion: The default texture of land_missing_base_default_v1 in an exterior cell is the colour texture (TX00, or its material's diffuse under ltex_texture_set_material_diffuse_v1) of the single texture set named by some LTEX's TNAM whose editor ID contains, ignoring ASCII case, both the editor ID of the cell's worldspace and the word default. With none or several, the default stays refused.
origin: Candidate from editor IDs only: nothing in the installation names the default. Offline indication (this installation): none of 2,049 GMST names a landscape or default ground texture; the installation's default and quality .ini files have no such key; no WRLD subrecord, and no 4-byte-aligned value of any other non-LAND record (2,146,031 scanned) resolves to an LTEX, apart from 16 scattered values in INFO, MESG, TERM and NAVM data. Of the 74 texture sets that LTEX name, one has default in its editor ID, and it contains the editor ID of one of 13 worldspaces (the main one); it has no TX00, and its material's diffuse decodes. Its two LTEX carry 20 vertex weights in all LAND, while the default carries 83% of all ground weight. In that worldspace, merging the default with it changes none of 4,473,014 shared seam vertex pairs where the default has weight (the seams cannot tell); comparing terrain LOD tiles over 131,563 default-only quadrants ranks it first of 74 texture sets, by 0.0001 RMS, a comparison that finds the right texture for only 5 to 10 of 349 single-texture quadrants, so it does not discriminate either. In the test exterior cell, 64 placed draws (ground meshes and decals) use its diffuse texture.
live_measurement: In one launch, photograph a quadrant without BTXT next to a placed ground object that uses this texture; then load an overlay plugin that points the texture set's MNAM at a material with a distinctive diffuse and photograph the quadrant again. If the default ground does not change, the rule is refuted.

assertion: A placed actor's skeleton root is placed by its ACHR DATA (position and ZYX rotation, as REFR DATA under refr_rotation_zyx_v2) and its ACHR XSCL (absent read as 1, as refr_absent_xscl_identity_v1); no NPC_ or RACE size field is applied.
origin: Candidate from the stored data: ACHR DATA is 24 bytes in all 10,391 winning ACHR; 5,183 of 5,678 exterior placements lie in their cell's grid square (4,096 units) and all 31,173 angles are within 2 pi. NPC_ NAM4 and NAM6 and RACE DATA hold further floats whose role is not established; they are reported, not applied.
live_measurement: In one launch, place two copies of one actor base with XSCL 1 and 2 and one with a NAM6 changed by an overlay plugin; measure getpos and the height of the head above the ground from screenshots: the first pair must differ by the factor 2 and the third must not differ from the first.

assertion: A templated actor base (ACBS u16 at 14 not zero) takes its race, ACBS bit 0, skin and outfit either from itself or from the templates its set bits name (TPTA slot k for bit k, TPLT without TPTA), recursively; a leveled actor list (LVLN with LVLD, LVLM and LVLF zero) yields one of its LVLO entries. When every such candidate gives the same value of a property, that value is the actor's.
origin: Candidate. Offline: in all 3,281 NPC_ with TPTA, bit k of ACBS u16 at 14 is set exactly when slot k is not zero (all 16 bits); which bit governs which property is not established, so every candidate is kept.
live_measurement: Place an actor whose own race differs from its template's with each template bit toggled by an overlay plugin; the race drawn in game tells which bit governs it. For a leveled list, place one whose entries differ only in skin and check that one of the entries appears.

assertion: A placed actor wears the armours of its NPC_ DOFT outfit (OTFT INAM: ARMO entries, and the single ARMO that every entry of a leveled item list with LVLD, LVLM and LVLF zero gives).
origin: Candidate. Offline: OTFT INAM is 4n bytes in all 477 OTFT and its 902 values resolve, 607 to ARMO and 295 to LVLI; NPC_ also carries SOFT (24 records) whose role is not established.
live_measurement: Place an actor with a DOFT outfit of one ARMO and give its SOFT another; photograph it standing in daylight: the DOFT armour must be worn.

assertion: An actor whose ACBS u32 at 0 has bit 0 set is drawn with its race's skeleton of the FNAM section (the ANAM after FNAM) and with each addon's MOD3; with bit 0 clear, the MNAM section's ANAM and MOD2.
origin: Candidate from token correlations only. Offline: among 197 untemplated NPC_ whose voice is one of two distinct race VTCK slots, bit 0 is set for 25 of 26 using slot 1 and for none of 171 using slot 0; the slot-1 VTYP editor IDs of 20 races add the same word that the FNAM-section egt paths of 98 races add, and of the 646 ARMA whose MOD2 and MOD3 differ, 607 have an f in MOD3's differing part and none in MOD2's (3 the reverse). In the 36 races whose two sections name different skeletons, both MOD2 and MOD3 models fit the MNAM-section skeleton (229 and 143 shapes with every bone found) and not the FNAM one (14 and 9), so the skeleton half of this rule has no offline support there.
live_measurement: Place two actors of one race and outfit differing only in ACBS bit 0 and photograph them: the one with the bit set must show the MOD3 models.

assertion: A worn ARMO draws every ARMA among its INDX/MODL pairs whose RNAM or MODL races include the actor's race.
origin: Candidate. Offline: every one of 1,019 ARMO stores INDX then MODL pairs; for the ARMO's own RNAM race, 818 ARMO have one such addon, 199 have two to sixteen and 2 none.
live_measurement: Photograph an actor wearing an ARMO with two addons for its race and with each addon's model replaced in turn by an overlay plugin: both must show.

assertion: An addon of the actor's skin armour is not drawn when its BOD2 word shares a bit with the BOD2 word of a worn outfit armour.
origin: Candidate. Offline: BOD2 is 4 bytes in every ARMO and ARMA; 1,094 of 1,387 addon BOD2 words have no bit outside their ARMO's word.
live_measurement: Photograph an actor wearing a body armour, then the same actor after an overlay plugin clears that armour's BOD2 bits: the skin body must appear only in the second.

assertion: A skinned shape's vertex is drawn at the sum over its non-zero weights of weight times the bone's node world transform in the pose applied to the bone's stored skin-to-bone transform of the vertex position.
origin: Candidate. Offline: the four binary16 weights sum to 1 within 0.001 in 19,090,505 of 19,090,725 skinned vertices of all NIFs (220 are all zero); with each model's own bone nodes the composite transforms of 4,585 of 5,081 measured shapes (4,759 within 0.1) are one translation shared by every bone of the shape within 0.01 units, so the blend of the bind pose moves the stored vertices rigidly.
live_measurement: Compare a screenshot of a posed actor (for example after a fixed idle) with a render of the same pose from the bone transforms read in game; a vertex blend that differs (for example dual quaternions) shows at bent joints.

assertion: The Havok skeleton an actor's animation clips are bound to is the first hkaSkeleton of the .hkx file at its skeleton NIF's path with .hkx for .nif.
origin: Candidate. Offline: of the 45 .hkx files at the path of a skeleton NIF that a RACE names, the composed reference poses put 1,962 of the 2,139 bones named in both within 0.01 units of the NIF node's world translation, and the dog skeleton all 65 bones within 0.0002; 15,861 of 16,145 clip bindings fit at least one of these skeletons. The clip itself does not name a skeleton file.
live_measurement: With an overlay that replaces one race's skeleton .hkx by a copy whose bone order is permuted (bindings index bones by position), play a known idle in game: the actor must break exactly as the permutation predicts.

assertion: A clip poses an actor by bone name in model space: each skeleton NIF node named like a bone of the Havok skeleton takes the bone's transform composed from the clip's local transforms (bones without a track keeping their reference pose), every other node its parent's pose after its own stored local transform.
origin: Candidate. Offline: the Havok reference pose composed this way matches the skeleton NIF's world transforms (1,962 of 2,139 bones of the race skeletons within 0.01 units) although the NIF names another parent for 163 of them; untracked bones and unnamed nodes are a choice that no stored value settles.
live_measurement: Freeze an actor in a known clip in game (pause during a fixed idle), capture it beside a render of the same clip time; compare silhouettes and the positions of extremities (hands, feet, tail) at two times.

assertion: A placed actor shows the models of the head parts (HDPT MODL) that its NPC_ lists in PNAM, or with no PNAM its race's HEAD of its section (after NAM0 and MNAM or FNAM), every one unmorphed and untinted (NAM0/NAM1 morph files, TNAM texture sets, face morph and tint fields of NPC_ not applied), each skinned to the actor's skeleton in the pose of the body. Every template and leveled candidate must give the same list. A listed part with conditions (CTDA), or a worn outfit addon skinned to a bone that the head parts use and no skin addon of the actor uses, leaves the head out; HNAM extra parts not listed are not drawn; a part whose skin names a bone the skeleton lacks is left out alone.
origin: Candidate. Offline (spec/actor.md, Heads): 420 HDPT, MODL in 419; PNAM a small integer and never repeated in one NPC_ list except 0, which marks the parts that other parts name in HNAM (DATA bit 3 set in those 154 and 2 more); the HNAM extras of listed eyes, hair and facial hair parts are listed too in 6,070, 2,329 and 1,113 cases and not in 76, 109 and 16, those of the face part in 305 and not in 1,695; 40 HDPT carry conditions (hair 30, eyes 10). Head part models are skinned to the race skeleton with the bind translation of the body addons; 297 of 313 shapes (model and skeleton pairs) name only skeleton bones; the others name hair cloth bones and three other bones the skeleton lacks.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed actor without morphs (its NPC_ with no face morph or tint fields) from the front beside its drawing: face, eyes, hair and beard must sit where drawn within a few units; then the same actor with a hat whose addon is skinned to the head bone: whether the hair is still drawn decides the covering clause.

assertion: A leveled actor list (LVLN) whose LVLD and LVLM are zero yields one of its LVLO entries whatever its LVLF byte (1 to 4): when every entry of such a list, followed as under npc_appearance_candidates_agree_v1, gives the same race, ACBS bit 0, skin, outfit and head part list, that look is the actor's. A list whose LVLD or LVLM is not zero stays refused.
origin: Candidate. Offline (spec/actor.md, Leveled bases and disagreeing candidates): over 375 LVLN, LVLD is 0 or 100 (9), LVLM always 0, LVLF 0 (81), 1 (17), 2 (66), 3 (206) or 4 (5); LVLG (a GLOB) in 14 lists, 9 of them the LVLD 100 ones. Of the 4,962 placed actors refused for a non-zero byte, the lists they reach have LVLD 0 for all but 19, and following every entry settles the look of 1,376 (LVLF 3: 1,285, 1: 77, 2: 14); none with LVLD 100 would settle. What LVLF selects (levels, counts) is not established and is not used: only lists whose entries all agree are drawn, so the choice cannot change the look.
live_measurement: Place, by an overlay plugin, an actor whose base is an LVLF 3 list of two NPC_ that differ only in skin; reload the cell several times: if one of the entries always appears, the rule's premise (one entry, its look) holds; then a list of identical entries must always show that look.

assertion: A templated NPC_ whose ACBS u16 at 14 sets every bit that any winning NPC_ sets (bits 0 to 5 and 7 to 12) takes every appearance property from its templates: its own race, ACBS bit 0, skin, outfit and head part list are no candidates.
origin: Candidate, the reading of npc_appearance_candidates_agree_v1 (own values or the templates their set bits name) when no bit is clear, whatever bit governs which property. Offline: of the 3,231 placed actors whose candidates disagree, the templated NPC_ of 33 all set every bit; leaving their own values out settles 10 (race), and the other 23 still disagree among their templates' leveled entries.
live_measurement: Place, by an overlay plugin, an NPC_ with every template bit set whose own RNAM, WNAM and DOFT differ from its template's; photograph it: it must show the template's race, skin and outfit.

assertion: Opcodes 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 store into slot 0 the integer sum, difference, product, quotient and remainder of slots 1 and 2; opcodes 2, 4, 6 and 8 the float sum, difference, product and quotient; opcodes 11 and 12 store into slot 0 the integer and float negation of slot 1. Integer overflow, an integer quotient or remainder of operands whose signs make the rounding convention matter, and a float quotient by zero are not decided (undetermined in fo4-vm); an integer division by zero stops the run.
origin: Candidate meaning recognised from prior knowledge of the format. Supported, not established, by spec/vm-checks.txt: slot 0 declared Int or Float as the operation says in every instruction; with slot 0 as destination no temporary is read before it is written, with no destination or another slot 2 to 720 such reads per opcode; array loops advance their index by opcode 1 with 1 in 555 of 562; executing 343 functions that reach no native, exchanging 1/3 and 2/4 makes 6 runs grow an array without bound and the candidate none. Exchanging product and quotient (5/7, 6/8) changes 8 results and fails no check: that part is not supported by any check run.
live_measurement: A hand-assembled test script (a loose .pex attached by an overlay plugin to an activator in a purpose-built cell) runs the opcodes on known operands and shows each result through a notification call when activated; any result other than the rule's rejects it.

assertion: Where a conditional jump, opcode 10 or a conversion to Bool tests a value that is not a Bool, an Int or Float is true when not zero, a String when not empty, an object or struct handle when not none, an array when not none and not empty; none is false. Whether an empty array is true is left open (the run blocks).

origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge of the native names and parameter names (apKeyword, iMaxExpectedLinkedRefs); built on vm_host_linked_ref_xlkr_v1. script_run --census PLACED: 288 chains answered with references, 69 empty, 52 counts, 2 loops left open.

assertion: ObjectReference.IsDisabled answers the record header flag 0x800 of the receiver's winning record (the flag the store reads as initially disabled), unless the same run enabled or disabled it.
origin: Flag recognised from prior knowledge, already read by fo4_plugin (Children.disabled); host_data_census: 4,032 placed records carry it (2,914 REFR, 1,050 ACHR, 67 PHZD, 1 PGRE), read and indexed alike in all 2,001,939 placed records. script_run --census PLACED: 133,317 calls answered.
live_measurement: Show IsDisabled of an initially disabled and an initially enabled reference through a notification call before anything enables them.

assertion: ObjectReference.GetBaseObject answers the record NAME of the receiver's winning record names; for the census's placement of a base alone, that base.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; fo4_plugin already resolves NAME as the base. host_data_census: every one of 1,789,365 placed REFR and ACHR has exactly one NAME of 4 bytes naming a winning record.
live_measurement: Show GetBaseObject of a placed reference compared with a property holding its base through a notification call.

assertion: Game.GetFormFromFile(id, file) answers the winning record defined by the plugin of that name in the load order (compared without case) with object id id masked to 24 bits (12 for a light plugin), none when no such plugin is loaded or no such record exists.
origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge of the native and parameter names (aiFormID, asFilename); the answer depends only on the manifest's load order. script_run --census PLACED: 394 calls answered with a record; ALL: 45.
live_measurement: Call GetFormFromFile for a record of a loaded master, of a plugin not loaded, and an id with a load-order byte set, and show the results through a notification call.

assertion: GlobalVariable.GetValue answers the f32 of the GLOB's single FLTV subrecord.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; host_data_census: every one of 1,916 GLOB records has exactly one FLTV of 4 bytes, all finite (1,893 integral); 549 carry header flag 0x40, whose meaning is not read. script_run --census PLACED: 670 calls answered; ALL: 221.
live_measurement: Show GetValue of a global never set by a script through a notification call, then of one set in an earlier session.

assertion: FormList.GetSize answers the number of the FLST's LNAM subrecords, GetAt(i) the record the i-th names in stored order (from 0), HasForm(form) whether one of them names the form; HasForm is undetermined when it is not found and the list holds other lists.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; host_data_census: 1,060 FLST, 12,548 LNAM all 4 bytes, 12,539 naming a winning record (94 of them a FLST).
live_measurement: Show GetSize, GetAt(0) and HasForm of a stored list through a notification call.

assertion: A record handle is of the engine script type its record type maps to (ACHR Actor, REFR ObjectReference, QUST Quest, GLOB GlobalVariable, KYWD Keyword, FLST FormList and the 31 others listed in fo4_vm::data::SIGNATURE_TYPES), with its parents and the scripts attached to it, and of no other type: a type test against another type is false.
origin: Table recognised from prior knowledge; host_data_census checks every VMAD object value (alias -1) naming a winning record of a listed type against the declared type of its property: compatible (the type, a parent, or a script extending it) in 35,882 values, not in 19 (13 REFR in Scene properties, 2 REFR in Quest, 1 REFR in Faction, 1 REFR in Perk, 1 QUST in ObjectReference, 1 NPC_ in Actor); 2,502 values name records of types not listed.
live_measurement: Test in a script a placed activator against Furniture and Activator and a quest against Quest, and show the results through a notification call.

assertion: A quest's VMAD scripts live on the quest's handle, the scripts of a quest's VMAD alias entry on that alias's handle, and a placed reference's scripts (base VMAD, then its own) on its handle, each with its VMAD property values, in its auto state, every other variable at its initial value, as if no event had run on it; a run attaches them when it first needs an instance on that handle.
origin: Interpreter assumption built on vmad_reference_scripts_v1 and vmad_property_sets_variable_v1; the QUST block is read to its last byte in all 1,353 QUST VMADs (spec/vmad.md). script_run --census PLACED: 2,614 quests, 47 aliases and 2,898 references given scripts; the 1,040 handlers blocked on an object without a script before are 1 after.
live_measurement: A hand-assembled activator script reads a property of a quest script and of an alias script and shows them through a notification call.

assertion: A VMAD object value whose alias word is not negative names the alias of that index of the quest its FormID names (one handle per quest and index), not a record.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; vmad_census: all 9,756 such values name a winning QUST; their properties are declared ReferenceAlias (7,536), RefCollectionAlias (816), LocationAlias (178) or Alias (7), never an object reference type; the quest's ALST values hold the index in 9,362 of 9,756.
live_measurement: Give a script a property naming an alias of a running quest and show the alias's reference through a notification call.

assertion: A save file is the magic, a header framed by its size word, a screenshot of width x height x 4 bytes, a form version byte, a game version text, a plugin block framed by its size word, a location table of six offsets, four counts and fifteen reserved words, global data tables 1 and 2, the change-form table, global data table 3, the form id array, a second u32 array and a closing block reaching the end of the file, each at the offset the table declares.
origin: Layout recognised from prior knowledge of the format; held by spec/save-census.txt: 8 of 8 files framed to the last byte (41,556,124 bytes), every declared offset equal to the sequential position (48 of 48).
live_measurement: Have the running game write new saves in several situations (new game, interior, exterior, after installing and after removing a light plugin) and read each: any file refused or framed differently rejects the rule.

assertion: Header fields in order: version, save number, character name, level, location name, play time text, race editor id, sex, experience, experience for the next level, a Windows file time of the save, screenshot width and height.
origin: Candidate meanings recognised from prior knowledge; only widths and framing are measured (spec/save-census.txt: text shapes, value ranges and the file time within 10 s of the file modification time in 8 of 8).
live_measurement: Write two saves of one character a level apart in the running game and compare each header field with the load menu and the character screen.

assertion: The screenshot is width x height pixels of four bytes in red, green, blue, alpha order, rows from the top.
origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge; held only in that the fourth byte is 255 in 1,966,080 of 1,966,080 pixels. Channel and row order are not measured.
live_measurement: Save in front of a scene with one large area of a known primary colour and compare the decoded pixels with the load-menu thumbnail.

assertion: The first list of the plugin block names the full plugins in load order (top byte of a runtime form id = index); the second names the light plugins in slot order (top byte 0xFE, slot in bits 12 to 23).
origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge; first list equal to the manifest's load order in 56 of 56 names; second list names end .esl in 54 of 54 (none installed, so slots are unchecked).
live_measurement: Install two light plugins, place one object from each in a test cell, move both in the running game and save: the change forms must name ids whose slots follow the second list's order.

assertion: A change-form entry is three reference bytes, a u32 flag word, a type byte (low six bits the type, top two bits the length width: 0 u8, 1 u16, 2 u32), a version byte, two lengths of that width and the first length of payload bytes.
origin: Layout recognised from prior knowledge; held by spec/save-census.txt: 55,319 entries end exactly at global table 3's declared offset in 8 files, width code minimal in 55,319 of 55,319, each reference once per file.
live_measurement: Read a save written after moving one placed object in the running game: exactly one more entry naming that object must appear, framed the same way.

assertion: When the second length is not zero the payload is a zlib stream whose output is that many bytes; when it is zero the payload is stored.
origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge; held by spec/save-census.txt: 17,305 of 17,305 exact zlib streams with the declared output length; no stored payload of 38,014 starts with 0x78.
live_measurement: Same saves as save_change_form_entry_v1: the payload of a heavily changed actor must inflate exactly before and after it changes size class.

assertion: The three reference bytes are a big-endian 24-bit word; top two bits 0: a 1-based index into the form id array, 1: a runtime form id with top byte 0, 2: the value with top byte 0xFF; kind 3 unused.
origin: Kinds recognised from prior knowledge; byte order and index base decided by spec/save-census.txt: 53,466 entries name a winning record, all with the record type of their change-form type; the 0-based reading names a record of another type in 2,512 entries and the little-endian readings name a winning record in 4,936.
live_measurement: In a purpose-built cell, move a placed object of the first master, a placed object of a DLC and drop an item, then save: the three change forms must name those forms under the rule (kinds 1, 0 and 2).

assertion: The form id array holds runtime form ids in the save's load order: top byte an index into the first plugin list, 0xFE a light slot, low 24 bits the object.
origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge; spec/save-census.txt: 60,405 of 62,866 entries name a winning record of the plugin data, 1,731 a light slot of a plugin not installed, 730 are zero, none unresolved; non-zero entries distinct.
live_measurement: Same saves as save_ref_id_kinds_v1: the DLC object's entry must carry that DLC's index in the first list.

assertion: Change-form types name record types: 0 REFR, 1 ACHR, 6 CELL, 7 INFO, 8 QUST, 9 NPC_, 28 ECZN, 30 FACT, 35 SMQN, 36 SCEN, 39 PHZD, 42 FLST, 44 LVLI, 49 INNR; types 4 and 43 name no installed record.
origin: The existence of such a numbering was known in general; the table is measured: under save_ref_id_kinds_v1 each type names a single record type in all 53,466 entries that name a winning record.
live_measurement: Change one form of each record type in the running game (move a reference, change a cell, finish a dialogue line, advance a quest) and save: each new entry must carry its type.

assertion: For change-form types 0 and 1 with flag bit 1 the payload begins with a reference to the cell or world the record is in, three f32 of position and three f32 of rotation in radians.
origin: Candidate recognised from prior knowledge; spec/save-census.txt: 8,922 of 8,922 payloads hold 27 bytes with finite, bounded values; the reference names a CELL or WRLD in 8,881 (the rest created forms or light slots); for plugin REFR the position is within 128 of the plugin DATA position in 78 of 78 and the reference names the plugin cell's world in 78.
live_measurement: Move a placed object by a known offset in a known cell with the console and save: the payload's first bytes must name that cell and hold the position and rotation the console reports.

assertion: A WAVE or XWMA sound file is RIFF: the four bytes RIFF, a u32 little-endian size equal to the file length minus 8, a form type, then chunks of a four-byte id, a u32 size, that many bytes and one pad byte after an odd size, filling the file to its last byte.
origin: Public container convention recognised from prior knowledge; held by spec/audio-census.txt: 170,463 of 170,463 sound entries (whole files and voice-container audio halves) framed to the last byte, 79,494 pad bytes all zero.
live_measurement: Write a RIFF file with an extra chunk and an odd chunk without its pad into an overlay archive in place of a looping ambient of a purpose-built cell and record whether the game plays each; a file the rule frames that the game refuses, or the reverse, rejects it.

assertion: The fmt chunk holds u16 format tag, u16 channels, u32 sample rate, u32 average bytes per second, u16 block align, u16 bits per sample, then, when longer than 16 bytes, a u16 count and that many extension bytes ending the chunk.
origin: Public wave-format layout recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: 2,467 chunks of 16 bytes and 167,996 of 18 bytes with count 0; for PCM the average equals rate times block align in 2,467 of 2,467.
live_measurement: Same overlay as audio_pcm_layout_v1 with the sample-rate field halved: the game's output must play at half pitch or half speed.

assertion: Format tag 1 is integer PCM and tag 0x161 a WMA-family codec; tags 2 and 0x11 (ADPCM) would be the coefficient-table and IMA-style ADPCM variants; none of tags 2, 0x11 or 0x162 occurs.
origin: Tag numbering recognised from prior knowledge. Tag 1 is supported for PCM by the step checks of audio_pcm_layout_v1; tag 0x161 is only a label: its files are counted and framed, not decoded, so nothing here could refute its meaning.
live_measurement: Record the game's output while a looping ambient of each tag plays in a purpose-built cell and compare its spectrum with the decoded PCM file (tag 1) and with a reference recording (tag 0x161).

assertion: A tag-1 data chunk is a run of frames of block-align bytes, one sample per channel in channel order, each bits/8 bytes of little-endian two's complement.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: data length a whole number of frames in 2,467 of 2,467 files; the little-endian signed reading has smaller steps between consecutive samples than the big-endian reading in 2,466 of 2,466 non-silent files and than the offset-binary reading in 2,466 of 2,466; a dump re-encoded from the decoded samples has a data chunk identical to the source's.
live_measurement: Record the game's output while a PCM-only looping ambient plays alone in a purpose-built cell and cross-correlate it with the decoded samples: no peak at the loop period rejects the rule.

assertion: In an XWMA file the data chunk is a whole number of packets of block-align bytes.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: data length a multiple of block align in 167,996 of 167,996 XWMA files and voice-container audio halves (2,421,939 packets).
live_measurement: None on the data alone: needs a decoder, which is out of scope; the packet count against dpds below is the only check.

assertion: The dpds chunk of an XWMA file holds one u32 per packet: the count of decoded 16-bit PCM bytes up to the end of that packet.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: dpds entries equal whole packets in 167,996 of 167,996; strictly increasing in 161,084, the others only because the last entry equals the one before (6,910) or, in 2 files, an earlier one; last entry a multiple of 2 x channels in 167,996; the data length over the stored average bytes per second agrees with the duration this rule implies within 10% in only 6,231 files.
live_measurement: Time the game's playback of a long XWMA music track from start to loop and compare it with the last dpds entry over 2 x channels x rate.

assertion: A voice container is FUZE, a u32 version, a u32 byte count of the lip half, the lip half, and the audio half, a RIFF file running to the file's last byte.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: 158,065 of 158,065 files split so, version 1 in all, every audio half an XWMA file read to its last byte; 6,244 lip halves are empty.
live_measurement: Put a voice container whose lip half is emptied into an overlay archive for one line of a purpose-built dialogue and observe that the line plays with the lips still.

assertion: A smpl chunk is nine u32 words, the eighth a loop count and the ninth a byte count of trailing data, then that many loops of six u32 words (cue id, type, start, end, fraction, play count) and the trailing bytes; start and end are frame indices of a loop the game repeats.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: 935 of 935 smpl chunks framed exactly; 901 loops, start <= end and end below the frame count in all, end = frames - 1 in 343; word 2 equals floor(1e9 / rate) in only 70.
live_measurement: Record a looping PCM ambient with a loop shorter than its file in a purpose-built cell: the repeat period must equal end - start + 1 frames.

assertion: A cue chunk is a u32 count and that many points of six u32 words, ending the chunk.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: 173 of 173 framed exactly; nothing reads the points.
live_measurement: None planned: the points are not used.

assertion: A LIST chunk is a four-byte list type and a chunk sequence filling the rest of its payload.
origin: Recognised from prior knowledge; spec/audio-census.txt: 1,257 of 1,257 framed exactly (types INFO and adtl); the contents are not read.
live_measurement: None planned: the contents are not used.

assertion: Four-byte FormIDs tie sounds to the world: CELL XCAS to ASPC, XCMO to MUSC, XCCM and each word of XCLR to REGN, XLCN to LCTN; LCTN NAM1 and WRLD ZNAM to MUSC; REGN RDMO to MUSC and every 12th byte of RDSA from 0 to SNDR; SOUN SDSC, ASPC SNAM, DOOR SNAM and ANAM, ACTI SNAM and VNAM, WEAP YNAM and ZNAM and the words at bytes 73, 85, 89, 93, 97 and 101 of the 132-byte WEAP DNAM to SNDR (zero allowed); ASPC BNAM to REVB and RDAT to REGN; ACTI RADR word 0 to SOPM; MUSC TNAM and MUST SNAM words to MUST; SNDR DNAM, SNAM and a 4-byte BNAM to SNDR, GNAM to SNCT, ONAM to SOPM.
origin: Field names from the published record naming; offsets and targets measured by spec/audio-census.txt: every non-zero slot of every listed field names a live record of the stated type (61,004 slots naming the target, 3,166 zero, in MUST SNAM, ACTI RADR and WEAP DNAM only; none names another type or no live record); the WEAP DNAM words were found by scanning every byte offset (787 values; the words at 77 and 81 are zero in all 480 records). What each link does in the game is not measured.
live_measurement: In a purpose-built cell, place one sound marker, one door and one region whose sound descriptors name distinct test files in an overlay archive, and record which file plays on entering, on opening the door and in the region.

assertion: A sound path stored in SNDR ANAM or FNAM or MUST ANAM or BNAM names a mounted file after removing a leading data folder; when no file has the stored .wav name, the same name with .xwm is the file.
origin: Readings tried in a fixed order and counted by spec/audio-census.txt: SNDR ANAM 13,213 of 14,016 resolve (2,592 as stored, 10,613 with .xwm, 8 only with a sound/ prefix added), MUST ANAM 527 of 575, MUST BNAM 20 of 20, SNDR FNAM 115 of 120; no path resolves under two readings; no stored path resolves to a voice container.
live_measurement: Replace one .xwm named by a sound descriptor of a purpose-built cell with a .wav of the stored name in an overlay archive and record which of the two the game plays.

assertion: An FNAM text of a material swap (MSWP) is an editor folder label: it neither selects nor conditions the swap's BNAM to SNAM substitutions, which apply as stored to every model that the naming reference or base draws.
covered_causes: RuntimeMaterialSwapFilter (MSWP FNAM, raised by the scene loader on the swap of a reference or base); the FNAM entries the draw build's swap reader then skips; render only (collision keeps mswp_collision_unchanged_v1)
origin: Reading recognised from general knowledge (an editor tree-folder field); kept because the swap_census of one installation could have refuted it and did not (spec/coverage.md, Material swaps): 1,901 FNAM in 1,482 of 3,935 winning MSWP, 54 distinct texts, every one letters, digits and backslashes shaped like a folder path, none four bytes or a FormID, 1,148 of 1,901 occurring inside a BNAM or SNAM path of the same record; stored before the first BNAM (1,072) or right after an SNAM (829); no record names an FNAM text as an editor ID other than 2 generic words. The substitution itself is path for path (no BNAM repeats within a record).
live_measurement: By an overlay plugin, place two references of one model naming two copies of one MSWP, one with its FNAM texts and one without, side by side in one purpose-built interior; photograph both in one launch: any difference in which material shows refutes it. Then change one FNAM to an unrelated text and repeat.

assertion: A surface's alpha (opacity) above 1, on a surface without blending, multiplies the sampled alpha before the alpha test exactly as values up to 1 do in the reference renderer, unclamped; it has no other effect.
covered_causes: UnsupportedRenderAlpha from an opacity above 1 with blending disabled (draw build, BGSM Alpha or NIF shader alpha); opacity above 1 with blending enabled stays refused
origin: No source; 34,815 placements of one installation are omitted for this alone (spec/coverage.md), 157 of 169 in the radius-2 test view with blending off, the alpha test on and opacity 1.7. With blending off, a clamp to 1 and no clamp give the same test result, so the rule decides only whether the opacity enters the test.
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed model whose material stores Alpha 1.7 with the alpha test on, then the same model through a loose material copy with Alpha 1.0: the alpha-tested silhouette must shrink as the rule predicts (texels with alpha between ref/(1.7*255) and ref/255 disappear); no change refutes it.

assertion: A base record's PRPS (pairs of an actor-value FormID and an f32) changes neither the model drawn for a placement nor where its collision is.
covered_causes: UninterpretedVisualSubrecord on PRPS of STAT, ACTI, FURN, CONT, FLOR, LIGH, MSTT and TERM bases (render and collision readiness)
origin: No source; measured on one installation with subrecord_probe (spec/coverage.md, Record properties): every PRPS of those types is a multiple of 8 bytes (2,139 records, 4,320 pairs); the first word of each pair is either a winning AVIF record (2,207, all with editor IDs naming workshop placement properties: bounds overrides, snapping, power, acoustic space) or a FormID below 0x800 of the base plugin with no record (2,113, engine-defined; their meaning is not in the data). 58,195 placements are omitted for this alone, among them the road pieces of the exterior test cell.
live_measurement: Place, by an overlay plugin, two copies of one road STAT side by side, one with its PRPS and one without (its value 0x33d = 1 removed); photograph both from above and walk onto both in one launch: any difference in shape, placement, texture or collision height refutes it.

assertion: A MISC base's CVPA (pairs of a component FormID and a count) changes neither the model drawn for a placement nor where its collision is.
origin: No source; measured on one installation with subrecord_probe: all 679 CVPA are multiples of 8 bytes; every first word of a pair resolves to a CMPO record (33 distinct, editor IDs naming crafting components), every second word is a small integer (1 to 100). 27,953 placements are omitted for this alone.
live_measurement: Place, by an overlay plugin, two copies of one clutter MISC with and without CVPA side by side; photograph both and drop the player onto both in one launch: any difference refutes it.

assertion: A reference's XRFG (a FormID naming a reference group, RFGP) changes neither the model drawn for it nor where its collision is.
origin: No source; measured on one installation: all 70,763 XRFG are 4 bytes and name a winning RFGP (9,372 groups); an RFGP holds at most a short text (NNAM, in 7,666 of 9,368, typically a generic word), one reference (RNAM, 7,905) and in 9 records a pack-in (PNAM); none stores a transform, a model or a material. 33,371 placements are omitted for this alone.
live_measurement: Place, by an overlay plugin, a copy of a grouped reference without XRFG beside the original; photograph both and walk into both in one launch: any difference refutes it; then disable the group's RNAM reference by console and check that the grouped reference stays visible (it would refute a reading in which the group gates presence).

assertion: When a placed reference draws a model (or a SCOL part places one), the model's root node's own transform (rotation, translation and scale) is replaced by the placement: it is not applied, to the drawn shapes or to the collision placed through the root.
covered_causes: Static draw of placed references and SCOL parts (fo4_render::draw, depth-0 node) and the Target chain of fo4_scene::collision, for root nodes whose own transform is not the identity; no readiness change: at the facts and measured levels the root composes as the schema's node transform
origin: Reading recognised from general knowledge; supported only by editor bounds (spec/nif.md, Root node transform; root_transform_census): of the base records whose models have a rotated root and whose five composed boxes differ, the OBND fits the box with the root's transform left out for 455, every handling for 1, none for 55, and the applied root alone for none. No placed model has a translated or scaled root, so the translation and scale parts are untested. Collision against render does not discriminate (the root is the first factor of both chains).
live_measurement: Photograph, in one launch, a placed STAT whose model's root node is rotated (an asymmetric model, for example a sign) beside its drawing with the root applied and with the root left out from the same camera words; then place, by an overlay plugin, a copy of that model whose root rotation is zeroed in a loose NIF: if the game ignores the root, both look the same; walk into both to check the collision.

assertion: A NAVM record holds NVNM, then optionally ONAM, then optionally NNAM, then MNAM. NVNM is: u32 version (15), u32 magic, u32 world, u32 parent, then counted sections (u32 count each) of vertices (three f32), triangles (21 bytes), edge links (11), door links (10), cover segments (8), cover mappings (4) and waypoints (18), then the search grid (u32 divisions, two f32 sizes, six f32 bounds, divisions squared counted lists of u16 triangles), ending at the last byte.
origin: Section order, record and subrecord names recognised from prior knowledge (docs/provenance.md); element sizes and counts measured. spec/navmesh-census.txt: 12,557 of 12,557 live NAVM occurrences (12,403 winning, 154 overridden) read to the last byte, 218,520,167 payload bytes, none refused; every triangle vertex index below the vertex count; version 15 and the same magic word in all.
live_measurement: Write one test-cell navmesh back in this layout with one triangle removed into an overlay plugin and send an actor across that spot in the running game: it must route around the gap; a file the game refuses rejects the layout.

assertion: NVNM word 2 is zero for a mesh of an interior cell, whose word 3 is the parent CELL FormID; otherwise word 2 is the world FormID and word 3 holds the cell grid as two i16, x in the high half and y in the low half. Vertices are world positions.
origin: spec/navmesh-census.txt: 906 of 906 interior winning meshes name their group's parent cell; 11,497 of 11,497 exterior meshes name the world whose group holds the cell and its XCLC grid (x high, y low; the swapped reading holds for 360); 4,015,764 of 4,017,912 exterior vertices lie inside the cell's 4096-unit footprint (95% of the rest within 2.1 units).
live_measurement: Change word 3 of one exterior navmesh to a neighbouring grid in an overlay plugin and observe whether actors of that cell still find paths in the running game.

assertion: A triangle is three u16 vertex indices, three i16 edge words (edge i runs from vertex i to vertex i+1; -1 is no neighbour, otherwise a triangle of the same mesh unless its link bit is set), an f32 at bytes 12-15 and five flag bytes, kept raw except the link and cover bits.
origin: spec/navmesh-census.txt over the winning live meshes: 14,472,430 neighbour words, 14,472,412 named back by the neighbour and 14,472,342 across the same two vertices in reverse order; no edge word outside -1, the triangle count or (link bit) the edge-link count. Bytes 12-15 are the largest finite f32 in 4,462,003 triangles; the finite values do not follow the vertex heights. Byte 20 is zero in all.
live_measurement: As nav_nvnm_layout_v1: a removed neighbour word must cut the walkable surface for actors in the running game.

assertion: Triangle byte 17, bit i (0 to 2): edge word i is an index into the edge links, not a triangle index.
origin: Found by testing each flag bit against the edge-link count (not recalled). spec/navmesh-census.txt: in the winning meshes 419,992 flagged edges name each of the 419,992 edge links exactly once, every word in range. Bit 6 of byte 17 (set on about 1.79 million triangles) is not interpreted.
live_measurement: Clear one link bit of a seam triangle between two exterior cells in an overlay plugin: actors in the running game must stop crossing that seam there.

assertion: Triangle byte 19, bit i (0 to 2): edge i has a cover mapping; bits 3 to 7 are zero.
origin: Found by matching the bits against the cover mappings. spec/navmesh-census.txt: mappings per mesh equal the set bits in 12,097 of 12,403 winning meshes; 858,645 of 860,369 in-range mappings name an edge whose bit is set; bits 3 to 7 zero in every triangle.
live_measurement: None planned: cover use by actors is not measured here.

assertion: An edge link is u32 kind, u32 navmesh FormID, u16 triangle of that mesh and u8 edge of that triangle that links back. Kind 0 joins touching edges of two meshes; kinds 1 and 2 come in mutual pairs and mostly join distant edges of one mesh. What the kinds mean to an actor is not established.
origin: spec/navmesh-census.txt: 419,848 of 419,992 links name a winning live NAVM (144 name no record); 419,819 name a triangle in range; 419,739 are mutual, and in all of those the edge byte is the linked triangle's edge that links back; kind pairs 0-0 399,166, 1-2 and 2-1 10,284 each; 17,381 kind 1 or 2 links name their own mesh with end points at least 16 units from the linked edge.
live_measurement: Remove the kind-1 and kind-2 links of a purpose-built cell with a ledge in an overlay plugin and see whether an actor still drops down or climbs there in the running game.

assertion: A door link is u16 triangle, a u32 word kept raw and u32 FormID of a placed door reference.
origin: spec/navmesh-census.txt: 1,189 of 1,189 winning door links name a placed REFR of a DOOR; the triangle is in range in all; the door lies 16 to 256 units from the triangle's centroid for 1,100 of them; the word is the same value in all 1,196 occurrences.
live_measurement: Lock or disable a linked door in a purpose-built cell and see whether actors stop routing through it in the running game.

assertion: A cover segment is two u16 point words, a u16 data word and a u16 flag word; flag bit 15 starts a chain whose segments follow each other. Point, data and flag meanings beyond that are not established.
origin: Weak. spec/navmesh-census.txt: the first segment of a mesh has bit 15 in 11,345 of 11,345; a segment without bit 15 starts where the previous ends in 1,223,173 cases and not in 259,439; only 1,520,572 of 3,528,534 point words are below the vertex count (the others cluster at fractions of 65,535). Kept raw.
live_measurement: None planned: cover use by actors is not measured here.

assertion: A cover mapping is u16 holding triangle times four plus edge, and u16 index of a cover segment.
origin: Found by matching against the triangle cover bits. spec/navmesh-census.txt: 860,718 of 860,718 winning mappings name a segment in range and an edge below 3; 860,369 a triangle in range; 858,645 an edge with its cover bit set; 997,046 segments are named by no mapping.
live_measurement: None planned: cover use by actors is not measured here.

assertion: A waypoint is three f32 (a position), u16 triangle and u32 flags.
